chunks: Abu Ahmad Hani ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmood al-Abdi - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me via his chain - he elevated it - that Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both)

entered upon Ar-Rashid, so Ar-Rashid said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, inform me about the four temperaments. Musa (peace be upon him) said: As for the wind, it is a king that is patient and gentle; and as for blood, it is a servant that is bold, and perhaps the servant kills his master; and as for phlegm, it is a contentious adversary, if you block it from one side it opens from another; and as for 'Safra (bile), it is the earth, when it shakes it trembles with what is above it. So Harun said to him: O son of the Messenger of God, you bestow upon the people from the treasures of God and His Messenger.
ai.seo_question: What are the four temperaments according to Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) in his dialogue with Ar-Rashid?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) engages Caliph Harun al-Rashid in a dialogue that blends physiological observation with spiritual metaphor, characterizing the four humors as distinct entities—wind as a veiling king, blood as a rebellious servant, phlegm as a contentious rival, and bile as a trembling earth. This exchange highlights the Imam's intellectual prowess and his capacity to reveal hidden divine truths (*kunuz*) to the ruling authority, a theme central to the Abbasid-era Imams' interactions with the caliphs. The Caliph’s concluding remark acknowledges that such wisdom is not merely human knowledge but a distribution of the spiritual treasures of God and the Prophet.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-8 Abu Ahmad Hani ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmood al-Abdi - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of narrators who linked up to Musa ibn Ja’far (s), “Musa ibn Ja’far (s) was shown into the presence of Ar-Rashid.

Then Ar-Rashid told him, “O son of the Prophet of God! Tell me about the four kinds of temperaments.” Then Musa (s) told him, “The wind which is a king who puts up with his people and treats them gently. Then there is blood that is like a servant who incurs a loss that often kills his master. And there is phlegm that is a hard enemy. Whichever way you block it, it will find another way. Andthere is ‘Safra which is like the earth that will make everything on it grow.” Then Harun asked him, “O son of the Prophet of God! Do you bestow upon the people gifts from the Treasures of God and His Messenger?”
